Counterpoint Research published its latest report predicting that cumulative revenue from consumer wearables will exceed US$1 trillion by 2032, led by smartwatches and wireless earbuds. Details by category are as follows.

Smartwatches and wireless earbuds are expected to dominate the market

Counterpoint Research's report published today states: "The global consumer wearables market is projected to generate cumulative revenue exceeding US$1 trillion between 2026 and 2032"

Within consumer wearables, the report forecasts earbuds will account for the largest share of cumulative revenue at approximately US$360 billion, followed by smartwatches at US$304 billion, and smart glasses at US$168 billion.

The report's breakdown is as follows:

Health patches are projected to generate US$120 billion, followed by smart rings at US$44 billion, pendant devices at US$24 billion, smart shoes at US$18 billion, and fitness bands at US$14 billion. Smart socks, smart clothing, and smart belts are each expected to generate less than US$10 billion.

Counterpoint Research notes that revenue growth in consumer wearables is twice that of shipment growth, or more notably, the market appears to be shifting gradually from fitness trackers toward preventive health—"where devices alert users before they notice a problem themselves."

When it comes to Apple, the company is already competing in the two highest revenue categories forecast by the report, including AirPods and Apple Watch. In addition, Apple is widely reported to be developing smart glasses, while also reportedly exploring a screenless fitness band and a smart ring.

Last month, Apple reported wearable, home and accessories category revenue of US$7.88 billion for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, a year-on-year increase of 6% and the strongest growth in the category since the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2022.

Admittedly, the category covers more than just wearables, but Apple's push as a strong revenue source in this space has continued for years; Counterpoint estimates that AirPods alone will surpass US$100 billion in cumulative revenue by 2026.
